subject: Science
title: Wet and dry
objectives: Children will test which materials get wet and which stay dry.
Children will notice that wet things dry in the sun.
content: Testing which materials get wet and which stay dry, and noticing that wet things dry in the sun.
teachingActivities: Let children test with a spray bottle or a dripping sponge; use the words wet and dry for every result; hang cloths in the sun and look again later; keep water use small and controlled.
learnerActivities: Test which materials get wet and which stay dry and see that wet things dry in the sun.
resources: Paper, cloth, plastic, foil and a leaf
assessment: Observe whether each child says wet or dry after testing and notices a wet cloth drying in the sun.
expectedOutcomes: Says wet or dry for materials after testing.
Notices that a wet cloth dries in the sun.

lessons.title: What gets wet?
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will test which materials get wet.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have explored water and know wet and dry, and have noticed the sun and rain.
resources: A spray bottle or a cup of water
lessons.starter: Sprinkle a few drops on a piece of paper and say "Look, it is wet."
teacherActivities: Show how to put a few drops of water on each material.
Let each child test a material.
Feel the wet paper and the wet cloth.
learnerActivities: Child puts water on a material and watches.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to put a few drops of water on each material. Children: Children watch and say wet.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child test a material. Children: Child puts water on a material and watches.
Step 3. Teacher: Feel the wet paper and the wet cloth. Children: Child touches and says wet.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "Which things get wet?" Children: Child points to the materials.

practical.title: Wet test
steps: Put a few drops of water on each.
practical.safety: Use only a few drops of water and wipe the tray. Supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Drop the water together and feel the material.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find another thing that gets wet.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says wet for materials that get wet
lessons.conclusion: Wipe the tray and hang the wet things to dry.
lessons.homeConnection: Test what gets wet in the sink at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "test which materials get wet" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: What stays dry?
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will find materials that stay dry in water.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have explored water and know wet and dry, and have noticed the sun and rain.
resources: Plastic, foil, a raincoat and a plastic bag
A spray bottle or a cup of water
lessons.starter: Sprinkle water on a raincoat and say "The water rolls off. It stays dry."
teacherActivities: Show how water rolls off the raincoat.
Let each child test plastic and foil with a few drops of water.
Feel the material under the water.
learnerActivities: Child puts water on the material and watches.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how water rolls off the raincoat. Children: Children watch and say dry.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child test plastic and foil with a few drops of water. Children: Child puts water on the material and watches.
Step 3. Teacher: Feel the material under the water. Children: Child touches and says dry.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Raincoats keep us dry." Children: Children say the sentence.

practical.title: Dry test
steps: Put a few drops on each.
practical.safety: Use only a few drops of water and wipe the tray. Do not allow children to put plastic bags near their faces.

differentiation.support: Drop the water together and look at the material.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to guess before testing.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Why do we wear a raincoat?

expectedOutcomes: Says dry for materials that keep water out
lessons.conclusion: Wipe the tray and put the materials away.
lessons.homeConnection: Test which materials keep water out at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find materials that stay dry in water" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Drying in the sun
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will see that wet cloths dry in the sun.
successCriteria: Hangs a wet cloth in the sun
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have explored water and know wet and dry, and have noticed the sun and rain.
resources: A washing line or a rack
lessons.starter: Hold a wet cloth and say "This cloth is wet. How can we make it dry?"
teacherActivities: Dip a cloth in water and squeeze it.
Hang the cloth on the line in the sun.
Feel the cloth after a short time.
Compare with a cloth left in the shade.
learnerActivities: Child hangs the cloth with help.
Child feels the cloth and says wet or dry.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Dip a cloth in water and squeeze it. Children: Child squeezes the cloth.
Step 2. Teacher: Hang the cloth on the line in the sun. Children: Child hangs the cloth with help.
Step 3. Teacher: Feel the cloth after a short time. Children: Child feels the cloth and says wet or dry.
Step 4. Teacher: Compare with a cloth left in the shade. Children: Child compares the two cloths.

practical.title: Drying cloths
steps: Dip a small cloth in water.
practical.safety: Keep the washing line low and clear of faces. Supervise water and pegs and keep children out of the sun at midday.

differentiation.support: Hang the cloth together and touch it later.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to guess how long it will take to dry.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is the cloth wet or dry now?
questions.expected: Wet at first and dry later.

expectedOutcomes: Notices that wet cloths dry in the sun
lessons.conclusion: Take down the dry cloths and fold them.
lessons.homeConnection: Hang wet clothes with your child and check when they are dry.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "see that wet cloths dry in the sun" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Wet and dry sort
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will sort materials into those that get wet and those that stay dry.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have explored water and know wet and dry, and have noticed the sun and rain.
resources: Two hoops labelled gets wet and stays dry
lessons.starter: Show two hoops and say "One is for things that get wet. One is for things that stay dry."
teacherActivities: Pick up a material we tested and ask "Does it get wet?"
Put it in the right hoop.
Let each child pick a material and sort it.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say wet or dry.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pick up a material we tested and ask "Does it get wet?" Children: Children say yes or no.
Step 2. Teacher: Put it in the right hoop. Children: Children watch and say wet or dry.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child pick a material and sort it. Children: Child sorts the material.
Step 4. Teacher: Check each hoop together. Children: Children name the materials.

practical.title: Sort by testing
steps: Put two hoops on the floor.
Pick a material and remember the test.
practical.safety: Keep materials dry for sorting. Supervise turns and keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Offer two materials and say the result.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a new material and test it.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Sorts materials into gets wet and stays dry
lessons.conclusion: Put the materials away and say "Wet and dry."
lessons.homeConnection: Sort things that get wet and stay dry at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sort materials into those that get wet and those that stay dry" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 5 wet and dry check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child tests and describes wet and dry.
successCriteria: Says wet or dry after testing
Notices a wet cloth drying in the sun
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have explored water and know wet and dry, and have noticed the sun and rain.
lessons.starter: Sing the wet and dry song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: wet test, dry test and drying cloths.
At each station ask "Wet or dry?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Child answers with a word or action.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: wet test, dry test and drying cloths. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "Wet or dry?" Children: Child answers with a word or action.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Wet and dry stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep water to a few drops. Wipe spills quickly.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one material.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to explain wet and dry to a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says wet or dry after testing; sorts materials; notices drying in the sun.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 5
Describes wet and dry with a word
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about wet and dry things at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child tests and describes wet and dry" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
